verdict.rationale: ObsessionDB documents a free developer tier: a no-credit-card dev instance of up to 4 vCPU and 8 GB that serves as a free sandbox. It also documents per-run branches of production data on isolated compute that can be discarded, and CHKit commands to validate and test pipelines as code. Together these give a free, non-production place to develop transformations, but there is no local engine or emulator, and the branching feature is framed around agent runs rather than the general developer loop. missing for 10: a documented local engine or offline emulator, evidence the dev loop is fast, branching documented for human developers rather than only agent runs, details on dev-tier limits and how dev work is promoted to production, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I get a fast local or free dev loop — a local engine, emulator, or sandbox — to develop transformations before touching production compute

citations.quote: Free developer tier. Spin up a dev instance to kick the tires. Up to 4 vCPU... No credit card required
Give each agent run its own branch of production data: isolated compute over the same S3. Let it experiment for real, then throw the branch away.
CHKit gives them typed commands to describe, validate, test, and deploy schema and pipelines as code
